item.text: {"question_id":"2B.4","answer":"During 2023, the government had formal civilian-protection and accountability measures: a victim-protection and reparations law, a presidentially chaired victim commission and fund, military ethics and conduct rules, commander commitments, relevant training, investigations, and strengthened cooperation with the ICC (BATCH-0029-E001; BATCH-0029-E002; BATCH-0011-E003; BATCH-0011-E004; BATCH-0019-E001). There was some operational and judicial follow-through: the government reported hospital treatment and an investigation after the Goma operation; security personnel were arrested, tried, and in some cases convicted, with a reparations order for recognized victims (BATCH-0023-E014; BATCH-0011-E018; BATCH-0011-E021). UNDP also reported new legislation, expanded justice access, investigative-capacity improvements, mobile-court convictions, and six convictions for conflict-related sexual slavery, although these results were externally supported and not individually attributable to Tshisekedi (BATCH-0009-E004). However, enforcement was inconsistent and materially inadequate. Monitors documented killings and other abuses by state forces amid widespread armed-group violence; the state of siege transferred civilian administration to military authorities and coincided with serious rights abuses (BATCH-0011-E009; BATCH-0010-E015; BATCH-0009-E002). In Goma, the official death toll was disputed, victims’ bodies and families were mishandled, investigations lacked autopsies and ballistic work, and the proceedings included convictions of soldiers but also flawed prosecutions of civilians and incomplete identification of responsibility (BATCH-0011-E018; BATCH-0011-E020; BATCH-0011-E021). The evidence therefore supports formal safeguards and some investigations, prosecutions, convictions, treatment, and remedy, but not reliable or comprehensive enforcement; attribution to Tshisekedi is direct for some legal and policy measures and indirect or uncertain for many operational acts.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0029-E001","BATCH-0029-E002","BATCH-0011-E003","BATCH-0011-E004","BATCH-0019-E001","BATCH-0023-E014","BATCH-0011-E018","BATCH-0011-E021","BATCH-0009-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E009","BATCH-0010-E015","BATCH-0009-E002","BATCH-0011-E020","BATCH-0011-E021"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not establish complete rules of engagement, prisoner-specific safeguards, operational logs, or nationwide enforcement outcomes.","Government-reported safeguards and claimed reductions are partly self-reported; several justice and training gains were externally supported.","Many abuses and accountability decisions are attributed to state institutions or military authorities rather than personally to Tshisekedi.","The Goma death toll and responsibility record remain contested, and investigations and appeals were incomplete or pending during the documented period."],"corrections_made":["Added the omitted favorable implementation evidence on commander commitments, military codes, training, judges, justice access, and convictions.","Specified that Goma produced reported treatment, investigations, prosecutions, convictions, and a reparations order, while preserving evidence of incompleteness and contestation.","Replaced the overly broad implication of uncertain remedy with a calibrated distinction between some demonstrated remedies and inadequate or flawed enforcement.","Clarified the 2023 period and separated direct presidential attribution from institutional or uncertain attribution."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A full ledger review could determine whether additional evidence directly addresses prisoner safeguards, rules of engagement, command responsibility, or nationwide remedy implementation.","The Goma evidence may require further reconciliation of official, UN, court, and independent casualty and responsibility findings."]}
